=== MULTI-SOURCE TOPIC CLUSTER: Volunteer pilots fly kitten with twisted legs from Omaha to Kansas State for treatment ===

[Source 1 — www.1011now.com] (URL: https://www.1011now.com/2026/10/27/volunteer-pilots-fly-kitten-with-twisted-legs-omaha-kansas-state-treatment/):
Stated Claim / Post Context:
Volunteer pilots fly kitten with twisted legs from Omaha to Kansas State for treatment

Volunteers are going a long way to improve life for a tiny kitten.

Actual Article Body:
OMAHA, Neb. (WOWT) - Volunteers are going a long way to improve life for a tiny kitten.

It took Muddy Paws volunteers a week to catch the kitten, named Serena. The 10-week-old feral kitten can only use half her paws.

“So, her legs are almost pointed, pulled backwards at this point. She walks on her hocks, but she gets around pretty well with them,” said Jessi Corbin, a rescue volunteer.

Corbin, a veterinary technician, says Serena has twisted leg syndrome. Experts at the Kansas State College of Veterinary Medicine will work to improve the kitten’s quality of life.

“So flying her down there and getting seen as soon as possible is so important,” Corbin said.

Volunteer pilot Bob Dyer met his tiniest passenger before the flight.

“Beautiful little kitten,” Dyer said.

Dyer and his wife, Vicki, donate the time and the cost of flying their plane from Millard Airport to Manhattan, Kansas, with Corbin and Serena on board.

“We are blessed to be able to own this and we just need to pay it back, and I love animals,” said Vicki Dyer.

Bob Dyer is an instrument-rated pilot. He says this will be his first cat, but not his first Angel Flight. He has flown dogs and people.

The flight takes about an hour and a half. After landing, Corbin sent photos of Serena in the care of veterinarians and vet techs at Kansas State. After treatment, Serena will be ready for adoption.

Muddy Paws Rescue is paying for the vet care at Kansas State.

Actual Article Body:
‘Americans from every state deserve fair and honest elections no matter what political party is in power,’ said Honest Elections Project Executive Director Jason Snead.

This November, voters in five states will decide more than who governs for the next two or four years. They will decide what rules will govern the 2028 presidential election.

That’s a key takeaway from a new report by Honest Elections Project Action (HEPA) on the stakes of this fall’s state legislative and gubernatorial elections. Published this week, the compelling analysis underscores how the outcome of these races will determine the integrity of elections in 2028 and beyond.

“With several states on the cusp of gaining trifectas, voters need to be aware of the radical agenda that Democrats will undoubtedly push, as demonstrated in Virginia, should they sweep in state legislatures,” Honest Elections Project Executive Director Jason Snead said in a statement. “Republican states have taken steps to ensure honest and fair elections for both parties, but every Democratic state trifecta has allowed lax voter regulations that create undue risks for fraud and damage public trust in outcomes. Americans from every state deserve fair and honest elections no matter what political party is in power.”

The HEPA report emphasizes the role state governments will play in shaping election laws for years to come. Not only will these governors and legislatures decide whether their elections are safeguarded by voter ID and other secure voting practices, but they’ll also preside over redistricting and Democrat-led efforts to subvert the Electoral College.

To paint a contrast between the parties, HEPA details how election-related bills passed by Republican trifectas during 2026 state legislative sessions focused heavily on “the fundamentals of secure elections.” This included advancing laws focused on proof-of-citizenship and eligibility to vote, cleaning voter rolls, enhancing voter ID requirements, and banning ranked-choice voting.

When it came to Democrat trifectas, however, the exact opposite occurred. The election integrity group notes how these leftist-run states passed laws promoting insecure mail-in voting practices, automatic voter registration, limiting “the use of citizenship data,” and implementing “fresh curbs on voter list maintenance.”

“Democrats defend each move in isolation as improving ‘access,’ but together they add up to a coordinated anti-election integrity agenda designed to tilt the playing field for pure political advantage,” the report reads.

[READ: Election Integrity Warrior Cleta Mitchell Drives The Left Crazy]

HEPA makes a point of highlighting that five states with gubernatorial and state legislative elections — Arizona, Michigan, Nevada, Pennsylvania, and Wisconsin — are also key battlegrounds that will determine the winner of the 2028 presidential election. Should Democrats win trifecta control of them in the midterms, the group warns, it “would mean California- and Virginia-style voting ‘reforms’” — many of which plagued the contested 2020 election — in these states for the next several elections.

HEPA’s analysis also emphasizes how other areas of federal importance are on the ballot this November.

States will have control over potential mid-decade redistricting efforts. Several states have redistricted their congressional maps within the past year in light of the Supreme Court’s Callais decision, which prohibited the use of race in the process.

Also at issue is Democrats’ National Popular Vote Interstate Compact, “whose members pledge to award their presidential electors to the winner of the national popular vote rather than their own state’s result.” The compact, which “purportedly takes effect at 270,” is 48 electoral votes shy of its goal, meaning that new Democrat trifectas in the aforementioned battlegrounds would give its supporters the numbers they need to “finish the job before the 2028 presidential election.”

“The pattern is not subtle. One side spent the year making it harder to cast an ineligible ballot and easier to keep the rolls clean. The other spent it dismantling those protections and enlarging the electorate on terms of its own choosing,” the HEPA report concludes. “When voters head to the polls this November they will be voting for more than governors and senators — they may well decide the future of free and fair elections in America.”

Twisted special ed teacher booked hotels for sex with teenage student

The victim said he and the teacher were "dating exclusively" when confronted.

Actual Article Body:
Switch between CA and NY editions here.

See more of our coverage in your search results.

A perverted Minnesota high school special education teacher repeatedly booked hotels to have sex with one of her teenage students.

Ann Margaret Bacon, 27, initially claimed that she didn’t start having sex with the 18-year-old boy until July 2023, a month after he graduated Tartan High School in Oakdale, just outside St. Paul, according to the Pioneer Press.

But she later confessed after she was confronted with a photo of them together at a hotel, where she also bought booze for other students who partied with them.

Records then showed that the teacher had booked a room at the same hotel at least four times — May 8, June 4, June 11 and even for the July Fourth holiday.

A witness said that the teacher and her pupil were known for “acting secretively” around each other — while another had explicit photos of both on his phone.

She also bought booze for minors, the witnesses said — with the criminal complaint noting one $40 Venmo payment she got that said it was for “liqq.”

The boy later told investigators that he and his teacher had been dating exclusively, and that he’d also stayed over at her apartment.

The teacher eventually admitted that she started having sex with the teen when he was a student, and that it actually ended, rather than started, in July 2023.

Bacon was sentenced to six months in jail on Monday after earlier pleading guilty to third-degree criminal sexual conduct involving a prohibited occupational relationship.

Bacon, who was hired as a special education at the high school in August 2022, resigned from her job in February 2024 on the same day she was interviewed by police, according to the Pioneer Press.
